name: Infinite Zoom
visualIdentity: Explicitly a camera and transition technique, not an art movement. Each world or scale is nested inside a visible object, lens, or portal; a continuous zoom reveals the next scene as the portal fills the frame. Match focus, scale, and velocity, and connect both composition and motion at loop points. The actual artwork and colors depend on the chosen worlds or reference.
suitableUses: Works for connected-world journeys, looping brand stories, surreal or abstract passages, kaleidoscopic transitions, and educational scale tours. Labels can make the journey explanatory. These are suitability judgments, not fixed style requirements; use it when nested worlds are meaningful content.
limitations: Dense text is hard to read during travel; keep labels in stable 2D space with reading holds. Avoid unplanned hidden resets, unstable orientation, or motion that conflicts with reduced-motion needs. A decorative spiral alone is not a scene handoff. A flat zoom is not a true 3D dolly; identify any 2.5D approximation. Omit unsuitable motion patterns when geometry or narrative does not support them.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. Resolve colors from task-provided exact colors, approved brand or reference palette, then existing semantic mappings; the supplied four-color example is optional only when none apply: background #F4EFE3, foreground #30404A, accent 1 #688D96, accent 2 #B78462. Use discrete tokens, no proposed gradient; accents are decorative and the supplied accent text pairings miss the normal-text contrast target. Preserve approved colors, roles, subject materials, and style color-family limits; check actual composites.
motionAndInteraction: Plan portals and transform chains at each scale; drive camera matrices from shared, seekable time and align portal coverage with the next scene. Continuous, coherent movement is appropriate, while preserving deliberate cuts, impacts, constant-speed travel, and reading holds. Interactive HTML may map finite scroll or pointer input to authored states; video must not depend on live input. Reverse and direct seeks must resolve consistently. Use candidate vortex, gateway, chapter, story, or dolly patterns only when their defining scene elements fit; a true dolly needs real depth or a disclosed 2.5D approximation.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Suggest music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor user choices and supplied assets. Let audio support the journey and leave room for reading or speech. Synchronize, mix, and inspect picture and sound together; avoid clipping and competing vocals.
assetRequirements: Prepare layered high-resolution assets or numbered frames with transparency, consistent dimensions, clear names, and a layer manifest. Inspect assets before composition; define each portal and scale handoff. Render sections separately if needed to control memory. Preserve colors and materials, and cache stateful simulations or provide deterministic replay. Do not claim simulated appearance is physical production.
combinations: Can stand alone when nested worlds carry the content. Style-027 contour line art scales cleanly: keep stroke weight stable, reserve accents for the next portal, and match loop composition and velocity. Style-097 annotations suit educational tours: keep labels fixed outside the zoom and use primary palette tokens. Avoid blurry raster textures and wildly changing detail density. Other motion patterns are optional and must match actual scene geometry and narrative.
productionApproach: Choose renderer and motion engine for visual fidelity and action before the export pipeline; assign one owner per animated property. Canvas 2D is the required style renderer; GSAP is the motion engine, with optional PixiJS for many 2D sprites and Three.js only when genuine 3D is needed. Use HyperFrames for composition, seekable timing, media/audio sync, checks, and export; Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, and record the reason. Drive all video state from composition time, load local assets, seed randomness, and inspect opening, transition, action, closing, loop, and audio sync. For interactive delivery, add accessible scroll or keyboard controls and reduced-motion behavior.
